entities.name: De rerum natura
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
De rerum natura (On the Nature of Things) is a didactic poem written by Lucretius around 100 BCE. 

 This epic work, spanning approximately 6 books and consisting of nearly 9,000 lines, systematically explores the philosophical ideas of Epicureanism.

 Through engaging narratives, vivid imagery, and lucid explanations, Lucretius presents his vision of an ideal society based on reason, the pursuit of pleasure without pain, and the rejection of superstition.

 De rerum natura is more than a philosophical treatise; it's a masterful work of literature that continues to captivate readers with its timeless themes and profound insights into human nature. 

 The poem addresses fundamental questions about existence, free will, the nature of the universe, and the role of humans within it, offering a unique perspective on these enduring concerns.

 De rerum natura is an indispensable part of classical literature, providing a rich source for scholars, philosophers, and readers alike. 

 Created by Lucretius. Dating to c. 100 BCE.
